one_line_description.value: AI meeting notetaker that records, transcribes and summarizes meetings; its public API exposes meeting summaries, transcripts and action items.
one_line_description.quote: Fathom summarizes your meetings so you can focus on the conversation.

has_public_api.quote: Fathom now has a public API that gives you developer‑friendly access to meeting insights so you can build workflows and integrations that connect Fathom with the rest of your tools.

api_breadth.value: Narrow, meeting-data focused: summaries, transcripts, action items, recording downloads, shared_with field; read-oriented with webhook delivery
api_breadth.quote: Build exactly what you need - bring meeting summaries, transcripts, and action items right into your own tools and workflows for a tailored experience.

docs_url.quote: Anyone can browse the API docs and start building!

auth_methods.quote: API keys and access: API keys are created at the user level. Your key can access meetings recorded by you or shared to your Team.

access_model.quote: In Fathom, open User Settings → API Access.

access_notes.value: API keys are self-created at the user level via User Settings → API Access; the Public API page states anyone can browse the docs and start building, and Fathom keeps a free individual plan. A separate partner/OAuth-app registration is needed only for a future marketplace listing. The MCP connector (distinct from the REST API) requires Fathom 3.0+ and a Premium or paid Team plan after trial.
access_notes.quote: Partners can register an OAuth app to be eligible for a future marketplace listing as a Fathom‑approved integration.

official_mcp_server.quote: To learn more about Fathom's MCP and how to connect it to any other MCP-compatible tool, visit api.fathom.ai/mcp.

rate_limits.value: 60 calls per minute across all of a user's API keys; no higher limits offered
rate_limits.quote: Rate Limiting: users can make 60 calls per minute across all of their API keys; this ensures system stability and reliability.

webhooks.quote: This guide will help you test whether your endpoint can successfully receive webhooks from Fathom.

verdict_reason: Fathom documents a public API for meeting insights, with user-level API keys created self-serve in Settings and OAuth apps for partners, plus a free individual plan. Rate limits (60 calls/minute per user across keys) and webhooks are documented, and the vendor also operates an official MCP server at api.fathom.ai/mcp. Scope is narrow (meeting summaries, transcripts, action items, recordings), but broad enough for useful read workflows.
open_questions: API protocol style (REST vs GraphQL) is not stated on the captured pages; the developer reference at api.fathom.ai was referenced but not fetched.
Canonical developer docs/quickstart URL was not captured; docs_url currently points at the official 'Public API' help article that references a Quickstart Guide.
OAuth scopes/permissions for the partner OAuth app flow are not described in the captured evidence.

Whether API key creation is available on the free plan or only on paid tiers is not explicitly stated; the pricing page lists 'Build custom integrations and workflows' without clear tier mapping. Release-note snippet (not citable text) suggests all users have API access.
No official SDKs were found in the captured sources; sdk_languages left null pending review of api.fathom.ai docs.
No versioning/deprecation policy found in the captured sources.
No Fathom-provided sandbox/test environment is documented; the 'Test URL' in the webhook guide refers to the customer's own receiving endpoint, not a Fathom sandbox.
MCP endpoint is published in text as 'api.fathom.ai/mcp'; the scheme (https) was inferred and the exact per-org configuration/auth details for non-Claude/ChatGPT clients are not captured.
MCP availability is plan-gated (Premium or paid Team plan after trial), unlike the base API — worth clarifying separately if MCP is a build target.
App disambiguation: confirmed as Fathom AI notetaker at fathom.video per the input hint, not other products named Fathom.
